course_description:
This course provides an introductory understanding of the concepts and practices of group work and teamwork, and of ways in which planners can achieve effective outcomes in negotiating and community consultation for desirable planning and development outcomes, especially as part of a planning team. Because urban planners work mainly in teams it is critical that students are aware of the issues that can arise in working within groups, including the approaches that different people take to decision-making and problem solving. The course will include a basic standard personality assessment and will then build on students' team experiences to include basic approaches to conflict management, ethical negotiation, community consultation and group dynamics.

This course provides first year planning students with insights on the significance of developing teamwork and negotiation skills. The course will provide conceptual discussions and practical activities to understand and develop teamwork and negotiation skills. In doing so, students will get skills to work proficiently as part of a team and individually in planning practice and learning activities. A ‘Teamwork Charter’ will be created in the course that will help students while undertaking professional and university teamwork.

restrictions: BRTP, BUPlan, BUPlan (Hons) and students taking an Urban Systems major only

timetable:
Additional timetable information
FIELD TRIP: A compulsory field trip will be held in Week 8. The field trip will visit the Woolloongabba Priority Development Area in Woolloongabba. Information gathered from the trip will inform the group assessment and role-play activities in week 11. Details will be provided in class and on Blackboard.
course_aims: This course aims to give students insights and knowledge to develop skillsﾠforﾠworking in planning-related teams.ﾠThe course will provide students with an understanding of teamwork dynamics, negotiation, and participation to produce better processes and outcomes within teams.

learning_outcomes.description: demonstrate an understanding of the roles and procedures of teamwork and negotiation in planning
apply individual skills for negotiation and conflict resolution for successful teamwork
design an agreed Teamwork Charter to facilitate teamwork within planning learning and practice
reflect on and assess your individual skills and capabilities to work as part of a team and individually
demonstrate an understanding of the professional values within the planning practice
identify and examine different roles and processes of stakeholder engagement in planning
analyse conflicts and challenges in planning and develop strategies for conflict resolution and negotiation
demonstrate well-developed communication skills for effective written and verbal communication

assessment_details.title: Stakeholder analysis (group assignment)
assessment_details.due_date: Group Report 30/10/2026 1:00 pm Submission via Blackboard
assessment_details.task_description: Assessment Rationale: Stakeholder Analysis Group Report For this assessment you will be presented with a real-world planning issue. Students form a group of 4-6 depending on final student enrolments. A final list of groups will be posted on the course Blackboard. Students work in the same groups for both report and presentation. Your group (your team) represents a stakeholder in a real-world planning scenario. The report will build on material gathered during the compulsory field trip in Week 8 where you will visit the Woolloongabba Priority Development Area in Woolloongabba, your pre-negotiation plan due in week 10 and the stakeholder negotiation exercise in week 11. Your group report will analyse the case study , identify and analyse the stakeholders involved, reflect about your role in the negotiation exercise and reflect about the overall negotiation experience. A nominated team leader from each group will submit a Group Report (2,000 words +or- 10% - excluding tables, figures, diagrams, images, references, appendices, endnotes and footnotes) - one copy per group. If, for whatever reason, you find that your group is not functioning effectively, please contact your Course Coordinator for support. assessment_details.task_description: Assessment Rationale: This course requires attendance and active engagement in the weekly workshops. In total, the course includes 12 workshops, and one field trip held in week 8. During the workshops, students will participate in various activities, typically in small groups. Attendance and participation in each workshop activities equate to 1 mark. You are required to attend and actively participate in 10 out of the 13 course workshops to achieve the full mark. There are two compulsory days to attend: the field trip in Week 8 where the class will visit the Woolloongabba Priority Development Area in Woolloongabba, and the role-play activity in week 11 . Note: While attendance and participation in the activities of all 13 workshops are recommended, it will not result in more than 10 marks dedicated to this assessment item.
